Q: Normalisation procedure in database A:

Here is one reference: https://www.freecodecamp.org/news/database-normalization-1nf-2nf-3nf-table-examples/#heading-the-third-normal-form-3nf

The Third Normal Form – 3NF When a table is in 2NF, it eliminates repeating groups and redundancy, but it does not eliminate transitive partial dependency.

This means a non-prime attribute (an attribute that is not part of the candidate’s key) is dependent on another non-prime attribute. This is what the third normal form (3NF) eliminates.

So, for a table to be in 3NF, it must:

  • be in 2NF
  • have no transitive partial dependency.

Also, on this Wikipedia page, you can see references to the original source text, and other references, and an example: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Third_normal_form

You want to turn off that behaviour when you are not in zen mode. To do so, press F1 and execute the command View: Toggle Centered Layout.

Q: Coder workspace container not able to connect to host docker socket (deployed via Docker Compose) A:

I managed to figure this out!

Here is the fix:

1. Coder UI: Use "Update and Restart" Doh. I should have clicked Update and Restart which actually pulls the new Terraform changes.

-->

2. Docker Socket Permission Mismatch Inside the workspace, the coder user (GID 1000) gets a permission denied error when touching the host's socket. Since this is a trusted, self-hosted environment, the workaround I used was to grant read/write access to the socket during the workspace boot sequence.

resource "coder_agent" "main" {
  os             = "linux"
  startup_script = <<-EOT
    set -e
    # Grant read/write access to the host docker socket to bypass GID mismatches
    sudo chmod 666 /var/run/docker.sock || true
  EOT
}

3. Idempotent mise Activation The mise tools were installing correctly to the persistent /home/coder volume, but they weren't being added to the PATH. You need to use the absolute path to mise when injecting it into .bashrc.

resource "coder_script" "install_tools" {
  agent_id           = coder_agent.main.id
  display_name       = "Install Tools"
  icon               = "/icon/terminal.svg"
  run_on_start       = true
  start_blocks_login = true
  script             = <<-EOT
    #!/usr/bin/env bash
    set -e

    if [ ! -x "$HOME/.local/bin/mise" ]; then
      curl -fsSL https://mise.run | sh
    fi
    
    # Temporarily export PATH so the script can use mise below
    export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$HOME/.local/share/mise/shims:$PATH"

    mise use -g dotnet@10.0 node@24

    # Inject into bashrc using the exact absolute path
    if ! grep -qs '~/.local/bin/mise activate bash' "$HOME/.bashrc"; then
      echo 'eval "$(~/.local/bin/mise activate bash)"' >> "$HOME/.bashrc"
    fi
  EOT
}

Once these are in main.tf, clicking Update and Restart results in a perfectly working workspace where docker ps, node, and dotnet all work!

This combination worked for me:

"editor.lineNumbers": "on",

Q: Mapbox navigation Ionic A:

I have asked this question to mapbox support if we can use ionic/cordova together with the mapbox native SDK and this is the answer.

  • Full turn-by-turn navigation features are only supported in the native Navigation SDKs for iOS and Android. If you only need to support route planning and show a list of maneuvers, you could use Mapbox GL JS or adopt Maps SDK for Flutter if you prefer to use a cross-platform framework supported by Mapbox.

  • If your use case requires full turn-by-turn navigation you must use the native SDKs.

  • This are the guides for both iOS and Android navigation SDKs

Q: Squashing commits after local/remote history diverged — best approach? A:

Run a single interactive rebase directly on your branch.

git rebase -i Y

Replace Y with the actual commit hash of Y

Your text editor will open. Change the word pick to squash (or just s) next to commit B, then save and close:

pick 1a2b3c4 A
squash 5e6f7g8 B
pick 9h0i1j2 C
pick 3k4l5m6 D

Once it is saved, you can just push your code like that.

git push --force-with-lease
